issue.title: date_input fails to initialize from sessionstate if today's date is not in the range [min_value, max_value]
issue.body:
### Summary

date_input fails to initialize from sessionstate if today's date is not in the range [min_value, max_value]
 
### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4884)

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit
from datetime import date
min_date = date(2029, 1, 1)
streamlit.session_state["with_min_value"] = min_date
streamlit.date_input("with_min_value", min_value=min_date, key="with_min_value")
```

or

```python
import streamlit
from datetime import date
max_date = date(2020, 12, 31)
streamlit.session_state["with_max_value"] = max_date
streamlit.date_input("with_max_value", max_value=max_date, key="with_max_value")
```

**Expected behavior:**
No error

**Actual behavior:**
StreamlitAPIException: The default value of <today's date> must lie between the min_value of ... and the max_value of ... inclusively.

No error is issued and date_input is correctly initialized from sessionstate if today's date lies in the range [min_value, max_value], for example:

```python
import streamlit
from datetime import date
min_date = date(2020, 1, 1)
max_date = date(2030, 12, 31)
streamlit.session_state["x"] = min_date
streamlit.date_input("x", min_value=min_date, max_value=max_date, key="x")
```


### Debug info
Streamlit, version 1.10.0
Python 3.10.4

comments.body:
Workaround: use additionally the argument value=<initial value> with date_input.
A warning is issued, but only once.

Thanks for reporting @clo-vis. You could argue that this is or isn't a bug, depending on your viewpoint.

In the [docstring](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.date_input), it mentions that the argument `value`:

> Defaults to today as a single-date picker.

Since you are specifying min and max dates, but not value, then the code fails because today's date isn't between those values.

However, you could argue in a case like these, `value` should equal `min_value` or `max_value` so that the code always works. I'll mark this as an enhancement to look into.

Best,
Randy

The [`documentation`](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/session-state#caveats-and-limitations) also says:

> Setting the widget state via the Session State API and using the value parameter in the widget declaration is not recommended, and will throw a warning on the first run

(this is my workaround currently)

The fact that streamlit wants me to set a valid initial value within [min, max] using `value` and the recommendation that I should **not** use `value` if I initialize the widget using session state is problematic for _number_input_ too.  This will fail with "The default value of 0 must lie between the min_value of None and the max_value of -1, inclusively.:

```python
streamlit.session_state["negnum"] = -1
streamlit.number_input("A negative number", max_value=-1, key="negnum")
```

> Since you are specifying min and max dates, but not value, then the code fails because today's date isn't between those values.

According to the documentation, min_date and max_date are used to specify the minimum and maximum **_selectable_** dates, not the minimum and maximum valid dates. Streamlit doesn't complain at all if I type a date outside the range (that is, without using the widget for date selection), so why complaining about an invalid initial value?

I am hitting this bug, too.

This works for other widgets:
```
import streamlit as st

if "some_number" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.some_number = 3

st.number_input("some_number", min_value=2, max_value=4, key="some_number")
```

But fails for `st.date_input`

```
import streamlit as st
from datetime import date

if "some_date" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.some_date = date(2023,1,1)

st.date_input("some_date", min_value=date(2023,1,1), max_value=date(2023,12,31), key="some_date")
```
That latter generates an exception:

```
StreamlitAPIException: The default value of [datetime.date(2024, 4, 8)] must lie between the min_value of 2023-01-01 and the max_value of 2023-12-31, inclusively.
```

@LukasMasuch As I was searching for this bug to report or upvote, I saw #8410 and am wondering if this bug might be accidentally nudging people into that "known limitation" of combining `value` and `key`.

@sfc-gh-dmatthews Yep, that indeed looks like that `date_input` is broken in this case. In the case of  number_input we are only checking this for `value` if it's not None: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/55bba786dcc8dd85e724746cd26bba3018a147bc/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/number_input.py#L377 In case of `date_input` it seems that we are doing this check after the default value is already set (to today) -> this is causing the issue.

I'm hitting the bug when typing in a date that is out of bounds. With @sfc-gh-dmatthews's code snippet it looks like this when changing the year to 2022.

The error appears before clicking out of the field, so you can stumble into it while editing the date.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ba364f0-0b88-4bdd-86f8-544d54fcad62)

Streamlit version 1.44.1
I think this issue can be closed. I cannot reproduce it on streamlit version 1.44.1. I have made a new bug report for the related issue in my previous comment.
@foldager Thanks for pointing this out! I also cannot reproduce the issue above anymore in the latest version of Streamlit.
